questions.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{5}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼\text{Exp}(\theta )$ and unknown rate parameter $\theta .$ For a particular sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{5},$ you're given that 

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{5}{x}_{i}=4.5.
$$

Find the likelihood function of the sample.

*Hint: The probability density function for an exponential random variable is given by* 

$$
f(x;\theta )=\theta {e}^{-\theta x},\,x\ge 0.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=5$ independent exponential random variables with unknown parameter $\theta ,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x;\theta )=\theta {e}^{-\theta x},\,x\ge 0.
$$

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}\theta {e}^{-\theta {x}_{i}} \\  & ={\theta }^{n}\,{e}^{-\theta \sum {x}_{i}} \\  & ={\theta }^{n}\,{e}^{-S\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

where $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}.$ 

We are told that $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}=4.5$ and $n=5.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\theta }^{5}\,{e}^{-4.5\theta }.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3}$ be I.I.D. random variables with probability density function

$$
f(x;\theta )=\theta {x}^{-\theta -1},\,x\ge 1,
$$

where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter. Find the likelihood function of the sample $4.1,\,2.5,\,2.8.$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=3$ independent random variables with unknown parameter $\theta ,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x;\theta )=\theta {x}^{-\theta -1},\,x\ge 1.
$$

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\theta {x}_{i}^{-\theta -1}) \\  & ={\theta }^{n}\cdot {\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{-\theta -1} \\  & ={\theta }^{n}({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i})^{-\theta -1}\end{aligned}
$$

For our sample, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} & =4.1\cdot 2.5\cdot 2.8=28.7\end{aligned}
$$

and $n=3.$ Therefore, 

$$
L(\theta )={\theta }^{3}(28.7)^{-\theta -1}.
$$

questions.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3},{X}_{4}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼N(\theta ,1),$  where $\theta $ is an unknown mean. For a particular sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4},$ you're given that 

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{4}{x}_{i}=8.98,\,{\sum }_{i=1}^{4}{x}_{i}^{2}=29.4.
$$

Given that the likelihood function of the sample is

$$
L(\theta )=\frac{1}{4{\pi }^{2}}\,{e}^{\,g(\theta )},
$$

what is the expression for $g(\theta )?$

*Hint: The probability density function for a normal random variable with mean $\theta $ and variance $1$ is given by* 

$$
f(x;\theta )=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-(x-\theta )^{2}/2},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=4$ independent normal random variables with unknown mean $\theta $ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=1,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x;\theta )=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-(x-\theta )^{2}/2},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}/2}) \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-\sum ({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}/2} \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-(\sum {x}_{i}^{2}-2\theta \sum {x}_{i}+n{\theta }^{2})/2} \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-(C-2S\theta +n{\theta }^{2})/2}\end{aligned}
$$

where $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $C={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2}.$

We are told that $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}=8.98,$ $C={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2}=29.4,$ and $n=4.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & =(2\pi )^{-4/2}\,{e}^{-(29.4-2(8.98)\theta +4{\theta }^{2})/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4{\pi }^{2}}\,{e}^{\,-14.7\,+\,8.98\theta \,-\,2{\theta }^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
g(\theta )=-14.7+8.98\theta -2{\theta }^{2}.
$$

questions.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3},{X}_{4}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼N(\theta ,1),$  where $\theta $ is an unknown mean.  Given that the likelihood function of the sample $0.3,\,1.2,\,-2.6,\,0.4$ is

$$
L(\theta )=\frac{1}{4{\pi }^{2}}\,{e}^{\,g(\theta )},
$$

what is the expression for $g(\theta )?$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=4$ independent normal random variables with unknown mean $\theta $ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=1,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x;\theta )=\frac{1}{\sigma \sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-\frac{1}{2}{(\frac{x-\theta }{\sigma })}^{2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-(x-\theta )^{2}/2},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}/2}) \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-\sum ({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}/2} \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-(\sum {x}_{i}^{2}-2\theta \sum {x}_{i}+n{\theta }^{2})/2} \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-(C-2S\theta +n{\theta }^{2})/2}\end{aligned}
$$

where $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $C={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2}.$

For our sample, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}S & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =0.3+1.2+(-2.6)+0.4 \\  & =-0.7 \\ C & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =(0.3)^{2}+(1.2)^{2}+(-2.6)^{2}+(0.4)^{2} \\  & =8.45\end{aligned}
$$

and $n=4.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & =(2\pi )^{-4/2}\,{e}^{-(8.45-2(-0.7)\theta +4{\theta }^{2})/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4{\pi }^{2}}\,{e}^{\,-4.225\,-\,0.7\theta \,-\,2{\theta }^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
g(\theta )=-4.225-0.7\theta -2{\theta }^{2}.
$$
